question: Can certified unused optional arguments be omitted without changing effective native behavior, and is this a genuinely untested intervention worth a new original-benchmark trial?
answer: Native equivalence passes, but the proposed mathematical intervention duplicates an already closed three-arm projection study. The only additional field set is two flags on parallel-thinking. This extension has no observed tool-call exposure in the eight project executions from the two latest studies. Do not execute the proposed15-cell trial or present this as a new tested actor strategy.

knowledge_adaptation.fact: Earlier optional_parameter_projection removes exactly detailed/allow_variables inMiddle and detailed/show_ast/check_balanced/max_depth inLate. Native and actor execution were already unchanged in that study. It had a simultaneous semantic_contract_direct ablation.
knowledge_adaptation.observation: In that study, ignored flags appear in baseline validation calls but in neither corrected-description nor projected calls. Thus removing them did not supply a unique observed suppression of these arguments beyond the correction control.
knowledge_adaptation.hypothesis: A structural schema intervention might still influence latent choice/context allocation, but current records do not establish that causal channel.

execution_and_budget.observation: The latest two project studies total8executions with zero thinking-tool calls. Stops document truncation/round exhaustion; they do not identify why output capacity was allocated that way.

Preserve the exact traceback, recover the full exception text, freeze the remaining302calls, and run them once. This is a diagnostic recording repair, not an actor/runtime change.

evaluation_uncertainty.fact: 27native invariants/controls pass, but no new agent completion or product was evaluated. Previous actor studies have one exposed execution percondition and same-coordinator review.
evaluation_uncertainty.limit: Neither333native calls nor0/8thinking calls prove that schema context cannot influence behavior. No causal efficacy, population effect or new Goal success is inferred.

literature.mechanism: Analyze whether arguments contribute to live uses; protect interfaces that cannot safely be transformed; remove dead arguments while transforming internal function signatures and call sites consistently.
literature.conditions: LLVM requires compiler IR, use-def/call-site information and visibility restrictions. It does not train an LLM or evaluate agent tasks.
literature.borrow: Use an explicit non-use/observable-behavior argument plus negative controls before treating omission as a canonical valid choice.
literature.difference: No LLVM pass or native program rewrite is implemented. We inspect a finite set of known JavaScript handlers/dispatchers and test the public MCP boundary; any proposed change would only affect model-visible knowledge. Invalid-value diagnostic behavior is outside omission equivalence.
literature.novelty_correction: This compiler analogy is new documentation, not new research novelty: the project's earlier optional_parameter_projection already implemented the same mathematical mechanism with20native admission calls and a three-arm actor experiment.
literature.reuse: Earlier projection research already pinned EasyTool2401.06201v3/JARVIS7624cf388b47334ff8a0868e7d862dde18cfda86 and distinguished its staged actor from our static interface projection. Existing A-MEM/ExpeL/ACE/Reflexion records remain valid; no full literature review repeated.

source_certificate.math: Both stages: dist/tools/handlers.js59-75 destructures only expression, parses it and formats the result. Middle server.js46-52 supplies defaults for two optional flags; Late46-79 validates types/range, requires allow_variables, and forwards otherwiseunusedoptionalflags. All valid optional choices can be omitted with identical handler behavior; required allow_variables remains.
source_certificate.parallel: Middle dist/index.js166-223 andLate303-360 read only pathId,thought,pathNumber,totalPaths,thoughtInPath,pathStatus,relatedPaths,readyForSynthesis. No dynamic argument lookup, whole-argument storage or spread occurs in this callback. convergenceDetected andneedsNewPath are schema-only options. Stored thoughts/status/timestamps are independent of them; relatedPaths is effective and retained.
source_certificate.limits: Manual known-version certificate, not a general JavaScript verifier. Native calls cover boolean omission/false/true combinations and max_depth omission/1/100 boundaries; source review supports other valid max_depth values. Timestamps need not be byte-identical across fresh processes, but flag values are not used to compute them.
